The dual-band metamaterial perfect absorber uses a metal–insulator–metal (MIM) structure with Ag disks and rings on a polyimide substrate.
Resonance peaks occur at 1.54 μm (near-IR) and 6.2 μm (mid-IR) wavelengths.
The 1.54 μm peak suppresses scattering signals used by laser-guided missiles.
The 6.2 μm peak matches a strong atmospheric absorption band for MWIR.
The absorber reduces 1.54 μm laser light scattering by more than 90%.
MWIR and LWIR signatures are suppressed by more than 92% using the absorber.
The absorber maintains over 90% IR signature reduction from room temperature to 500 °C.
The disk radius is optimized at 0.168 μm to align MP and SPP resonance peaks at 1.54 μm.
The period of the disk array is set to 1.34 μm to excite SPP Bloch waves at 1.54 μm.
The ring outer radius is 600 nm and inner radius is 500 nm to achieve the 6.2 μm MP resonance.
The top Ag metal layer thickness is 0.18 μm; the polyimide insulator layer thickness is 0.1 μm.
The absorber’s resonance peaks are insensitive to polarization due to circular symmetry of unit cells.
The full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of the 1.54 μm peak is 40 nm, ensuring narrowband absorption.
The 6.2 μm MP resonance peak has a broadband absorption with FWHM around 1 μm.
The absorber’s performance is stable for incident angles up to 10° at 1.54 μm and up to 50° at 6.2 μm.
Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations and inductor–capacitor circuit models (ICCM) closely predict resonance wavelengths.
Magnetic polaritons (MPs) arise from coupling between electromagnetic fields and magnetic resonances inside the MIM structure.
Surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) occur at metal–dielectric interfaces and produce nearly perfect absorption at specific wavelengths.
The absorber reduces thermal radiation emissivity in the long-wavelength IR (8–14 μm) range.
The dual-band absorber design prevents enhancement of short-wavelength IR (SWIR) signatures by having a narrow absorption bandwidth at 1.54 μm.
